title: Rumor:  Razor Lake gets 12 P-core only die with bLLC on Intel 18A-P
gist: Rumor (via leaker Jaykihn) that Intel's 2028 Razor Lake includes an unlocked 12 P-core-only (12+0+4, Coyote Cove) single compute die with bLLC built on Intel 18A-P, in contrast to Nova Lake whose top SKUs may be TSMC N2P-only; Razor Lake will still also have TSMC N2 variants.

insights.claim: Intel is reportedly preparing an unlocked Razor Lake desktop processor with 12 P-cores on a single compute die, built on Intel's 18A-P process and featuring bLLC (Big Last Level Cache), per hardware leaker Jaykihn.
insights.speaker: S
insights.so_what: An internal-node flagship-class client die signals Intel confidence in 18A-P yields/performance; watch for confirmation as a foundry credibility marker.
insights.quote: Intel is reportedly preparing an unlocked Razor Lake desktop processor featuring 12 P-cores on a single compute die.
insights.locator: Intel is reportedly preparing an unlocked

insights.claim: The rumored Razor Lake part uses a 12+0+4 configuration: 12 Coyote Cove performance cores, zero standard efficiency cores, and four low-power efficiency cores.
insights.speaker: S
insights.so_what: A P-core-heavy, no-standard-E-core design targets per-thread performance (e.g., gaming), a segment where Intel competes directly with AMD's cache-heavy parts.
insights.locator: Jaykihn reports that the processor has

insights.claim: The Razor Lake 12 P-core part is reportedly a dedicated P-core-only compute die rather than a hybrid die with disabled E-cores, and all 12 P-cores sit on one die rather than two six-core compute tiles.
insights.speaker: S
insights.so_what: Taping out a dedicated die implies Intel sees enough volume in the high per-thread-performance desktop segment to justify extra design cost.
insights.locator: The leaker clarified that this is

insights.claim: Coyote Cove, the P-core architecture in the rumored Razor Lake die, is also expected to debut with Nova Lake.
insights.speaker: S
insights.so_what: Core-architecture reuse across generations shifts Razor Lake's differentiation to process (18A-P) and cache (bLLC).

insights.claim: Building a high-end Razor Lake variant on Intel 18A-P contrasts with Nova Lake, whose highest-end SKUs are expected to be possibly exclusive to TSMC N2P, suggesting Intel is pulling flagship client silicon back to its own fabs.
insights.speaker: S
insights.so_what: Insourcing flagship client dies would raise Intel Foundry utilization and reduce TSMC wafer spend from Intel; a signal for both INTC foundry thesis and TSMC N2 customer mix.
insights.quote: This contrasts with Nova Lake where the expected highest end SKUs will/may be exclusive to TSMC N2P.

insights.claim: Razor Lake will still have TSMC N2 (possibly N2P) variants alongside the 18A-P die, so Intel continues a dual-sourcing strategy for client CPUs.
insights.speaker: S
insights.so_what: Dual sourcing persists, so TSMC retains some Intel client business through the 2028 generation.
insights.quote: Razor Lake will also have N2(P?) variants, as well

insights.claim: Razor Lake, Intel's successor to Nova Lake, will span desktop and laptop segments and is slated to go on retail sale in 2028.
insights.speaker: S
insights.so_what: Sets the 2028 window for when an 18A-P flagship client part would test Intel's process competitiveness in retail.
insights.locator: Razor Lake is the successor to Nova Lake
